title: Contratto Aperitif
about: Contratto is one of the historic houses of Canelli, the Piedmont town that gave Italy its sparkling Moscato. Giuseppe Contratto founded the firm in 1867, and beginning in 1899 the company spent about ten years hand-digging cellars more than thirty metres into the hillside beneath its headquarters, part of the “underground cathedrals” of Canelli now within the UNESCO-listed vineyard landscape of Piedmont. Since 2011 Contratto has belonged to Giorgio Rivetti and his brothers of La Spinetta, who revived the aperitivi and digestivi the house had stopped making in the late 1960s.

The label dates the Aperitif recipe to 1935. It draws on twenty-eight herbs, spices, roots and seeds, among them aloe, angelica, wormwood, safflower, cinchona, bitter and sweet orange, lemon, mandarin, hawthorn, clove, cardamom, liquorice, juniper, mint, rhubarb, sage, nettle and ginger. The botanicals are hammer-milled and cold-macerated for more than thirty-five days, then blended with an organic distillate of Italian wheat made in Cuneo and sweetened with beet sugar. Its orange-red colour comes from carrot and beetroot rather than dyes. The blend is chilled, slowly filtered and rested about forty days in stainless steel before bottling at 13.5% alcohol.

At 250 grams of sugar per litre it is the sweeter of the house’s two aperitivi. Orange peel, orange blossom and rhubarb lead on the nose; white stone fruit and marzipan follow on the palate, with a soft bitterness and a delicate note of gentian. Its importer pitches it as a natural stand-in for Aperol, so it belongs in the classic aperitivo-hour spritz, with prosecco and soda over ice.
